subject: Access onboarding: SSO assertions, SCIM mapping, IP dry-run
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Carla Nguyen <carla.nguyen@acmeinc.com>, sec-ops@acmeinc.com
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Access onboarding: SSO assertions, SCIM mapping, IP dry-run

Hi Carla / Acme SecOps team,

Thanks for the quick pickup on the onboarding request. I want to align on the access-control scope so we can lock a short dry-run before production cutover. Proposed scope for the dry-run (staging):

- SSO/SAML: verify SAML Audience and ACS endpoints; confirm NameID format (email vs persistent).
- SCIM provisioning: group-to-role mapping for two pilot groups (Engineering-Admins, Analytics-Readers).
- IP allowlist: one staging CIDR per region (US-west / US-east) for test traffic.
- Service accounts: confirm naming convention and short-lived token strategy for our staging worker.

Immediate asks from your side:
1) A minimal CIDR (or single IP) you can open to for staging (we prefer narrow /32 addresses).
2) Okta (or identity provider) admin contact and whether SCIM API token can be created for provisioning.
3) Any org policies we should mirror (session timeout, forcing MFA for service accounts, attribute transformations).

Attachments: I attached a one-page sprint map and a SCIM mapping primer. I’ll have Priyom follow up with a proposed runbook and cutover windows.

Proposed dry-run window: Tue, Jul 26 — 10:00–11:30 PT (can change if this conflicts).

Next steps: if you can confirm the three items above by EOD Thu (7/20) we’ll firm the invite.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Sr. Customer Success (Onboarding)
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs: acme-onboard-sprint-map.xlsx (spreadsheet), scim-group-mapping-guide.pdf (pdf)
From: Carla Nguyen <carla.nguyen@acmeinc.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: sec-ops@acmeinc.com, David Keller <david.keller@acmeinc.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access onboarding: SSO assertions, SCIM mapping, IP dry-run

Thanks, Irene — appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications from SecOps:

- IP allowlist: we cannot open wide CIDRs in prod. For staging a single /32 is fine but we need the exact egress IPs you plan to use. Can Redwood provide per-region egress IPs or a short list?
- Service accounts: we prefer short-lived credentials (<= 1 hour) where possible. How does your worker refresh tokens?
- SCIM mapping: we use Okta and prefer group-to-role mapping; we also need an attribute sent for department.

Also — for SAML assertions, our SAML engineer asked about the Audience value. Is the audience going to be the model endpoint host (e.g., api.redwood.ai) or an RP ID we should expect?

If you can answer those three bullets we’ll confirm the dry-run.

Carla Nguyen
Security Operations Manager
Acme Inc.

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Jul 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access onboarding: SSO assertions, SCIM mapping, IP dry-run

Carla — quick answers and a proposed operational plan below. Forwarding the sprint map and a runbook snippet for the dry-run.

1) Egress IPs: for the staging cluster we can give three static egress IPs (us-west-2: 52.34.12.101, us-east-1: 34.201.88.55) — these are our NAT egress addresses for the staging plane. For the dry-run we recommend you whitelist those two IPs as /32 entries. For prod we will discuss a more robust, multi-AZ list but we understand your need for narrow ranges.

2) Service accounts/token lifecycle: recommended pattern:
   - Name: acme-svc-redwood-<env>-<purpose> (e.g., acme-svc-redwood-stg-ingest).
   - Tokens: short-lived bearer tokens issued by our control plane with a 1-hour TTL; refresh via an OAuth refresh exchange.
   - For tasks requiring longer jobs we recommend a delegated refresh window with re-auth on >6h jobs (we can provide a default library for token refresh).

3) SCIM mapping: we propose the following attribute mapping for staging:
   - Okta group "ACME_Redwood_Eng_Admins" -> Redwood role "engineer:admin"
   - Okta group "ACME_Redwood_Analytics" -> Redwood role "analytics:read"
   - Send attribute: department (okta:user.department -> user.department)
   - Provisioning: incremental provisioning every 5 minutes in staging; full sync nightly in prod.

4) SAML Audience/ACS: Audience value should be set to https://api.redwood.ai/saml/consumer/acme (we will add the RP entry into your metadata). ACS will be the ACS endpoint in our tenant; we will provide the exact URL in the final metadata xml. NameID: we recommend email for pilot phase (easier mapping).

Proposed dry-run plan (summary):
- Thu, Jul 26 | 10:00 PT — Dry-run: confirm SAML assertion, SCIM group provisioning, and token-based service access from staging.
- Success criteria: (a) SCIM group maps to expected roles for three test users; (b) API call from an allowed staging IP succeeds and tokens refresh successfully; (c) no unexpected 401/403 during a 15-min smoke test.

Action items for Acme before 7/26:
- Provide confirmation of egress IP whitelist (or counterproposal).
- Create Okta SCIM API token and share it securely (we can accept in 1Password or HashiCorp Vault reference).
- Share an Okta admin contact for the provisioning test.

I attached the runbook snippet and the group-mapping pdf. If those look good we’ll send a calendar invite to lock time.

— Priyom Das
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
